ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, square $ABCD$ has a side length of 1, and point $E$ is on the extension line of $BC$. If $BE=BD$, then what is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square, \\
it follows that BC=CD=1, \\
By the Pythagorean theorem, we have $BD=\sqrt{BC^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{2}$, \\
therefore, $CE=BE-BC=BD-BC= \boxed{\sqrt{2}-1}$.
